rail_guard.text: Inverness Station, the northern end of the line. The Kyle line goes west to the sea, the Far North line goes up to Thurso, and the sleeper train goes all the way to London. Most of these trains have a view you'll talk about for a week.
Hop aboard. The Wildlore rail runs to any town you have visited in Great Britain. Where to?

verger.text: St Andrew's was built in the 1860s with a red stone front and two towers that never got their spires. It has a great ring of bells, a labyrinth path in the garden and a visitor who once asked if the cathedral was real. It is.
Please keep your voice down, we're a little shy. The pigeons, however, are not.

market_trader.text: Tablet, shortbread, fudge, and a Highland coo made of wool. Not that kind of coo, the other one. Well, also that kind.
The Victorian Market's been selling since 1870. The roof's been up longer than I have, and it's the more waterproof of the two of us.

dolphin_watcher.text: The dolphins come in with the tide, so I check the tide tables like other people check the football results. High water at Chanonry is the kick-off.
Our dolphins are bottlenose. They're the biggest in the world, because the Firth is cold, and a bigger body keeps the heat in. They are, in other words, wearing a very good jumper.

castle_walker.text: That's Flora MacDonald. She helped the Prince escape over the sea to Skye in a small boat, with him disguised as her maid. History has made a lot of her. The maid costume has got a lot of press, too.
Mind, the castle was the courthouse for years. Everyone still looks up at it nervously. It's the sandstone. It looks like it knows what you did.

ceilidh_dad.text: Fàilte to Inverness! We say 'Inbhir Nis' in Gaelic. It means 'mouth of the Ness', which tells you where to look if you're lost: downhill, towards the sea.
The Keeper's at the ice rink. Isla's a curler. If she says 'hurry hard', do as you're told. She's got a stone and a broom, and she knows how to use both.

gate_inverness.text: Closed for "seasonal rebranding". Skye and the Cairngorms, both. Sorry. I'm told it's temporary.
We're told it'll reopen once the Keeper at the ice rink has had a word with you. Up the hill, on the river. Ice rinks don't hide.
